Our culture 
At 1Password, we prioritize collaboration, clear and transparent communication, receptiveness to feedback, and alignment with our core values: keep it simple, lead with honesty, and put people first. 

You’ll be part of a team that challenges the status quo, and is excited to experiment and iterate in search of the best solution. That said, 1Password is not for everyone. Our work is demanding, we strive for excellence, and the pace is fast. We need people who are keen to take on challenging problems, who seek feedback to grow, and who are driven to make an impact. If you're looking for a place where you can settle into a comfortable routine, this might not be the right fit for you. We’re looking for individuals who are proven experts in their fields, as well as those who are highly adaptable, can thrive in ambiguity and through change, are curious, and above all deliver results.

Embracing the future of AI isn't just encouraged at 1Password—it's an essential part of how we will be successful at 1Password.

Our approach to remote work 
We believe in the power of remote work, but recognize that in-person connection is important to help us achieve our mission. How we’re using AI today

Our Engineering, Product, and Design teams are thoughtfully integrating AI across the full software and product development lifecycle to move faster without sacrificing quality or security. In practice, that looks like engineers using AI-assisted coding tools to accelerate reviews and catch bugs earlier, product managers synthesizing user research at scale, and designers rapidly prototyping and iterating with AI-generated mockups. We approach AI the same way we approach security: with clear principles, human accountability at every consequential decision point, and rigorous evaluation before anything ships to customers.

 You will work closely with management, customers, engineering, design, and commercial teams to understand what needs to be built, define how it should work, and ensure it is delivered successfully.
 A major part of your role will be translating product ideas and customer problems into clear requirements, workflows, tickets, acceptance criteria, and expected behaviours that engineering can execute against.
 You will own the detail behind the roadmap and ensure what we ship fulfils the original product and customer intent.
 Values 
 Excellent communication and collaboration skills
 Strong ownership and accountability
 Customer-focused and outcome-driven
 Highly organized with strong attention to detail
 Comfortable challenging assumptions and asking questions
 Open to feedback and continuous improvement
 High degree of integrity, professionalism, and discretion
 What You’ll Be Doing 
 Work closely with management to translate the Sadie product vision and roadmap into actionable product initiatives.
 Own and maintain the product backlog, ensuring priorities are clearly defined and aligned with the roadmap.
 Break larger product initiatives into clear requirements, user stories, workflows, tickets, and acceptance criteria.
 Define exactly how Sadie should behave across different customer scenarios and edge cases.
 Ensure engineering has the context and requirements needed to build features correctly without ambiguity.
 Work closely with engineering throughout development to answer questions, resolve ambiguity, make trade-offs, and keep delivery aligned with the intended product outcome.
 Review and validate completed work against requirements and acceptance criteria before release.
 Test Sadie across real-world scenarios to ensure features and behaviours work as intended.
 Review real customer calls, feedback, and product usage to identify gaps, edge cases, and opportunities for improvement.
 Work with customers and internal teams to understand problems and translate feedback into actionable product requirements.
 Coordinate product pilots and releases, including defining scope, expected behaviour, success criteria, and feedback loops.
 Identify dependencies, blockers, risks, and missing requirements before they impact delivery.
 Maintain clear documentation around product functionality, decisions, requirements, and expected behaviour.
 Track progress against the roadmap and communicate product status, blockers, and changes to relevant stakeholders.
 Ensure features are not simply shipped, but actually fulfil the original product vision and solve the intended customer problem.
 Continuously improve how requirements are defined, communicated, tested, and delivered across the product organization.
 What You Bring 
 2+ years of experience as a Product Owner, Business Analyst, or similar product-focused role.
 Experience working closely with software engineering teams to deliver customer-facing products.
 Strong ability to take a high-level product idea and turn it into detailed, actionable requirements.
 Experience writing clear product tickets, user stories, acceptance criteria, and functional requirements.
 Strong understanding of product workflows, user journeys, edge cases, and expected system behaviours.
 Experience managing and prioritizing a product backlog.
 Strong attention to detail and the ability to identify gaps or ambiguity before development begins.
 Ability to understand technical concepts sufficiently to communicate effectively with engineering teams.
 Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to make pragmatic decisions when requirements or priorities change.
 Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
 Ability to manage multiple initiatives and priorities in a fast-moving environment.
 Strong sense of ownership and accountability for the quality of the final product, not just the completion of tickets.
 Pluses 
 Experience working on conversational, voice, communications, or workflow products.
 Experience working with hospitality, restaurants, hotels, or other service-based businesses.
 Experience managing complex products with multiple integrations and dependencies.
 Experience working in a startup or fast-moving product environment.
 Comfortable working in an environment where the roadmap evolves quickly based on customer and business needs.
 Am I Right for This Position? 
 You will be a strong fit if you enjoy taking an idea that may initially be high-level or ambiguous and turning it into something an engineering team can confidently build.
 You should naturally think about questions like:
 What exactly should happen? What happens if something goes wrong? What are the edge cases? What does success look like? Does what we built actually match what we intended?
 You do not need to be an engineer. You do need to be comfortable working closely with engineers and taking ownership of the detail required to turn a product vision into a working product.
 Why Is This Job Important? 
 Sadie is evolving quickly, and our ability to execute on our product vision depends on turning ideas and customer needs into clear, well-defined work for our engineering teams.
 The Product Owner sits between vision and execution.
 Your responsibility is to make sure the roadmap does not remain a collection of ideas. It becomes clearly defined functionality that engineering can build, customers can use, and the business can measure.
 What Will I Learn in This Position? 
 You will gain hands-on experience building and scaling a rapidly evolving technology product used in real customer interactions every day.
 You will work closely with leadership, engineering, customers, and commercial teams and develop a deep understanding of how product strategy is translated into requirements, delivered through engineering, validated with customers, and continuously improved.

The Staff Product Manager is an Individual Contributor (IC) product leader responsible for a broad platform surface for Atlas Infinite at MongoDB. Atlas Infinite is the largest architectural innovation in MongoDB Atlas ever, purpose-built to handle today's speed and scale of development and demand. 
 In this position, you will own and solve end-to-end problems around the user experience and database experience of Atlas Infinite, including but limited to feature discovery, activation, monetization, and retention. You will see patterns, opportunities, and risks across areas, own cross-team product and architectural trade-offs, establish reusable standards for PM craft, and align senior stakeholders around multi-year bets. You have deep knowledge of cloud database platforms, distributed data systems, and enterprise product development.
 You will partner closely with cross-functional engineering leaders, product peers, and executive stakeholders to drive outcomes across organizational boundaries, guiding a portfolio spanning Atlas Infinite's disaggregated compute and storage architecture, production workload readiness, migration and Atlas interoperability, and the new customer experiences this architecture may make possible. You will not inherit a closed list of future features: part of your mandate is to discover opportunities we have not yet articulated and challenge assumptions about which problems matter most. With AWS public preview now live, you will help turn real workload evidence into a credible path to GA and subsequent releases, in close partnership with the existing team.
 This role can be based out of a MongoDB office or remotely in Canada.
 Responsibilities
 Interlinked Vision & Multi-Year Bets: Set and champion a product vision across Atlas Infinite's capabilities, while actively discovering opportunities that are not on today's roadmap or fit any single team's remit. Explore what decoupled compute and storage could make possible for developers, enterprises, and emerging AI workloads; use hypotheses, customer evidence, prototypes, and market signals to uncover needs we have not yet named. Branching, on-demand compute, and instant recovery are examples of possible bets. Make the case for investment and prioritization, including build-vs-buy considerations, and distinguish exploratory vision from release commitments
 Cross-Team Execution: Along with program management, own execution health across workstreams, negotiating sequencing, scope, and resource trade-offs with engineering leaders and peer PMs where you have no direct authority. Ensure preview-to-GA readiness, roadmaps, and dependencies across database, storage, Atlas platform, migration, backup, security, and cloud infrastructure teams are aligned and connect to company objectives
 Execution & Research Standards: Establish lightweight operating practices and shared customer/market research frameworks that make workload qualification, customer-representative testing, win/loss analysis, launch readiness, and post-launch learning consistent across the portfolio. Use data to drive decisions without overburdening delivery teams
 Product Health: Resolve complex post-launch escalations when the root cause spans architecture, performance, migration, observability, supportability, or unclear ownership. Turn customer and operational signals into systemic product fixes rather than one-off workarounds
 Customer Discovery: Identify needs and competitive dynamics that cut across product areas. Look beyond requests from today's customers to discover emerging jobs-to-be-done, surprising uses of the architecture, and reasons customers do not choose MongoDB at all. Combine interviews, workload and pricing evidence, product analytics, field feedback, and experiments to test known hypotheses and uncover unknowns; reorient the roadmap when the evidence warrants it
 Outbound & GTM: Partner with product marketing, pricing, sales, solutions architecture, customer success, documentation, and support on high-stakes customer engagements, product positioning, and omni-channel marketing. Establish ideal customer profile; ensure claims and migration guidance match demonstrated capabilities; translate successful adoption and enablement approaches into shared playbooks
 Executive Alignment: Synthesize customer experience, technical readiness, adoption, and commercial impact into clear, confident product stories for senior leadership. Surface cross-area risks and progress early, including trade-offs between new-workload growth, customer savings, and changes to existing Atlas usage
 Mentorship: Mentor PMs across the area, sharing frameworks for cross-team alignment, customer evidence, technical trade-offs, multi-year bets, and leadership communication
 Qualifications
 8+ years of product management or equivalent product leadership experience, with a track record personally shaping strategy and outcomes for complex technical platforms across multiple teams, rather than only coordinating delivery
 Strong technical fluency in cloud databases, distributed data systems, storage infrastructure, developer experiences, or an adjacent developer platform. Able to reason with engineers about architecture, performance, availability, data movement, and trade-offs without needing to be the system designer
 A demonstrated ability to discover opportunities beyond the current roadmap: connect technical possibilities to unmet customer needs, formulate and test hypotheses, notice surprising patterns, and change direction when evidence challenges the original thesis
 Experience taking a complex product from early adoption toward dependable, broader use while protecting space for longer-term innovation; able to make explicit trade-offs among customer trust, technical readiness, speed, and investment
 Proven ability to influence without authority, negotiating sequencing and resource trade-offs across partner teams with competing priorities
 Commercial and analytical judgment: able to assess workload-level value, adoption and usage evidence, competitive alternatives, pricing and unit economics, and the impact of a new product on an existing portfolio. Comfortable with build-vs-buy questions where relevant
 Ability to raise the quality of customer discovery and product decision-making across teams through useful shared methods and mentorship, without mistaking more process for better outcomes
 Exceptional communication skills: able to explain a technical and commercial thesis, its uncertainties, and the evidence that would change your mind to engineers, customers, executives, and go-to-market partners
 Success Measures
 In 3 months you will have built a shared picture of which workloads Atlas Infinite serves well today, where customers struggle, what must be true for broader adoption, and what remains unknown. You will have clarified ownership with peer PMs and engineering, established baseline measures, and identified the highest-value questions to investigate
 In 6 months you will have influenced consequential roadmap and GA-readiness decisions with customer-representative evidence; articulated a compelling, revisable view of where Infinite can create distinctive customer value beyond GA; and built a learning agenda with clear tests and decision points for both known bets and newly emerging opportunities
 In 12 months the portfolio will show measurable progress against its established baselines for qualified adoption, customer experience, and readiness for broader workloads. At Poka, we're changing how the world's industrial teams work — capturing the knowledge of their best people and putting it in every operator's hands. 
 Our connected worker platform is purpose-built for manufacturing and the wider industrial world, with industrial AI inside the shift, not on top of it. The result: frontline performance that becomes compounding knowledge and measurable impact — every shift, every site, every region. 
 We're proud to support global leaders like Nestlé, Bosch, Mars, and Danone across 3,000+ sites in 70+ countries. And as a fast-growing part of the IFS family, you'll join a team whose daily work directly shapes the platform behind how modern manufacturing gets done. 
 Role overview 
 Our team develops the AI assistant built into Poka. Workers and supervisors use it every day on manufacturing floors. We build it with prompts, tools, information retrieval and agents.
 As a quality assurance (QA) specialist on this team, you make sure what we ship works: the assistant's answers and the features around it. You do it with automation, AI and tools you build, not with manual testing. You work with the devs, the product team and the design team to define what "good" means, then you build the evals, automated tests and tools that check it.
 How this is different from traditional QA 
 No manual test passes. If something needs to be checked more than once, you automate it, with code, AI or whatever tool fits.
 A large part of what you test has no single answer. The same question can get 50 good answers phrased differently, and the assistant can answer differently from one run to the next. You help define what "good" means and measure it.
 You write Python every week.
 If you're looking for a role focused on test plans and manual regression testing, this isn't it.
 What you'll be responsible for 
 Automating QA for the team's features and building the tools that make it easier, including ways for non-developers to add evals and analyze the results.
 Building and maintaining eval suites based on real usage: actual user questions, expected behavior and the edge cases that show up in production.
 Defining with the team what a good answer looks like for our users, writing scoring rubrics and using LLM-as-judge where it makes sense, calibrated against human-labeled samples.
 Running regression checks in CI every time we change a prompt, a tool, retrieval or the Claude model version, covering answer quality, cost and speed. You build the guardrails, evals and tests that tell us whether a release gets the green light or not.
 Reviewing real conversations and grouping failures into patterns: made-up answers, wrong tool calls, missed context, inappropriate tone. Then working with developers to turn them into fixes.
 Contributing to adversarial testing: prompt injection, data leaking between customers, getting the assistant to do things it shouldn't.
 Doing timeboxed exploratory testing on features that change what the assistant can decide or do, like new agents, tools or actions, including checking that actions stay safe when something fails or gets retried.
 Joining feature kickoffs to help define acceptance criteria, including AI-specific ones.
 What you bring 
 AEC, DEC or BAC in a field related to the position, or equivalent experience
 2 to 4 years of relevant experience
 A background in test automation or as an SDET
 You're comfortable with several programming languages, including Python and TypeScript
 Real curiosity about how LLMs behave and why they fail
 You're comfortable judging quality when there's no single answer, and explaining your reasoning
 Curiosity about our users' world. You can't judge an answer without understanding what a supervisor on a manufacturing floor actually needs.
 Assets 
 You've helped set up an eval harness, even in a personal project
 Experience using AI tools to speed up testing
 Basic statistics: pass rates, variance, sample size
 Experience in security or adversarial testing
 Knowledge of the test pyramid and the shift-left approach
 B2B experience or experience on industrial platforms
 Knowledge of Jira
 The technologies you'll use 
 Python
 TypeScript
 Claude Code
 Eval framework (promptfoo)
 AWS
 Docker
 And many others

 Decide on the next steps needed to scale Meta Ads further through better creative

 Fully remote

 Proven VSL copywriting experience on DR / performance brands

 Meta VSLs: Proven experience with both short and long form Meta VSLs. Long form is the bulk of what we run.

 Deep fluency with DTC and modern consumer brands

 Tenstorrent is building the world’s fastest, most efficient AI compute clusters. TT-Fabric is the high-performance nervous system of this platform: the low-level networking layer that lets thousands of RISC-V and AI processors snap together into a single, massively parallel distributed supercomputer. If you love squeezing nanoseconds out of hot paths, designing protocols that move data at absurd scale, and turning messy hardware constraints into elegant distributed systems, this is an opportunity to shape the fabric that future AI models will run on
 This role is hybrid based out of Santa Clara, CA; Austin, TX; or Toronto, ON.
 We welcome candidates at various experience levels for this role. During the interview process, candidates will be assessed for the appropriate level, and offers will align with that level, which may differ from the one in this posting.
 Who We Are 
 Strong systems engineer with deep C or C++ experience and comfort working in low-level or bare-metal environments.
 Passionate about hardware-software interaction, performance tuning, and eliminating inefficiencies at the protocol level.
 Curious about networking, synchronization, and communication across large clusters.
 Comfortable reasoning from first principles and challenging industry conventions.
 Motivated by building infrastructure that directly impacts large-scale AI training and inference performance.
 What We Need
 Architect, implement, and maintain TT-Fabric, our low-level networking library powering distributed inference and training.
 Design scalable communication systems capable of coordinating thousands of AI processors efficiently and reliably.
 Optimize protocols, synchronization strategies, and data movement to extract maximum hardware performance.
 Integrate TT-Fabric APIs into the broader programming model in collaboration with AI and hardware teams.
 Help define the long-term architecture of Tenstorrent’s distributed systems stack.
 What You Will Learn 
 How large-scale AI clusters are architected from the networking layer up.
 The performance characteristics of custom AI hardware and RISC-V processors at scale.
 Advanced synchronization, collective communication, and interconnect optimization techniques.
 How distributed systems design decisions directly influence model throughput and training efficiency.
 How hardware and networking software co-evolve in next-generation AI infrastructure.

 GameSim is a game development studio that partners with clients to build games across PC/console and a range of art styles. We care about craftsmanship, collaboration, and shipping work we’re proud to put our names on. If you love building environments and believable spaces we’d like to meet you. Our headquarters is based in Orlando, FL!
 Talent Pipeline Posting Notice 
Please note that this posting is not tied to an immediate vacancy. We are proactively building a pipeline of qualified candidates in anticipation of potential hiring needs over the coming months. Applications will be reviewed and retained for future consideration as opportunities arise.
 We are seeking a Senior Lighting Artist to create high-quality real-time lighting and help guide lighting execution across GameSim projects.
 This is a hands-on senior role with leadership responsibilities. In addition to producing lighting work, you will review the work of other artists, provide clear direction and feedback, help organize lighting tasks, and ensure that scenes meet the visual and technical quality bar established by Art Direction and the client.
 You will collaborate closely with Art Directors, Environment Artists, Technical Artists, VFX Artists, Designers, Engineers, Producers, clients, and partner studios. You will help translate creative direction into practical lighting solutions that support mood, gameplay readability, environmental storytelling, narrative, and performance.
 This role may oversee the day-to-day work of other lighting artists or multidisciplinary artists contributing to lighting. It does not necessarily include formal people-management responsibilities, but it requires accountability for team output, effective mentorship, and the ability to raise concerns when work is at risk of missing quality, schedule, or technical expectations.
 What Success Looks Like
 Within your first 90 days, you will:
 Develop a clear understanding of the project’s visual direction, gameplay requirements, lighting pipeline, technical constraints, and production schedule.
 Build effective working relationships with Art Direction, Production, Technical Art, Environment Art, Design, Engineering, clients, and partner teams.
 Create polished lighting work that demonstrates the expected visual and technical quality bar.
 Take ownership of lighting for an assigned level, environment, sequence, or group of scenes.
 Review work from other artists and provide timely, actionable feedback that improves quality and consistency.
 Identify artistic, technical, or production risks early and work with project leadership to resolve them.
 Help the team deliver lighting work that meets milestone expectations for quality, performance, and completeness.
 Responsibilities
 Lighting Creation and Artistic Execution
 Create high-quality real-time lighting for gameplay environments, levels, cinematics, characters, and interactive sequences.
 Translate art direction, concept art, reference material, gameplay requirements, narrative goals, and client feedback into effective lighting solutions.
 Use lighting to establish mood, atmosphere, visual hierarchy, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Ensure lighting supports gameplay readability, navigation, combat visibility, character presentation, and important interactive elements.
 Develop and refine exposure, color, contrast, fog, atmosphere, reflections, shadows, emissive response, color grading, and post-processing.
 Create lighting for a range of visual styles, including realistic, stylized, cinematic, and highly art-directed projects.
 Maintain consistency across connected environments, gameplay spaces, cinematics, times of day, weather conditions, and lighting scenarios.
 Bring assigned scenes to final quality while meeting technical requirements and production deadlines.
 Leadership and Quality Oversight
 Oversee lighting work for an assigned area of the project, such as a level, world region, sequence, feature, or milestone.
 Review the work of lighting artists and other contributors whose work affects the final lighting result.
 Provide clear, constructive, and actionable feedback through live reviews, written notes, paintovers, reference boards, documentation, and in-engine examples.
 Ensure lighting work follows the visual direction, technical standards, and quality expectations established by Art Direction and the client.
 Help artists understand priorities, expected outcomes, acceptance criteria, and the level of polish required for each milestone.
 Track the visual progress of assigned lighting work and identify scenes that require additional support, revision, or escalation.
 Verify that feedback has been addressed and that completed work meets the established quality bar before submission.
 Mentor junior and mid-level artists in lighting fundamentals, technical execution, scene organization, optimization, and production practices.
 Lead by example through strong artistic execution, professional communication, reliable follow-through, and practical problem-solving.
 Help resolve differing artistic opinions by referring decisions back to approved visual targets, gameplay needs, technical constraints, and project priorities.
 Escalate unresolved quality, scope, staffing, scheduling, or technical risks to the appropriate project leads.
 Planning and Production Support
 Work with Art Direction and Production to break down lighting goals into clear tasks, priorities, estimates, and milestone deliverables.
 Help assess lighting scope, scene complexity, dependencies, and production risks.
 Support task assignment based on artist strengths, project priorities, and schedule needs.
 Provide progress updates and communicate when work is likely to miss visual, technical, or scheduling expectations.
 Participate in daily reviews, milestone evaluations, client reviews, and project-planning discussions.
 Help prepare lighting work for internal reviews, client presentations, milestone submissions, and final delivery.
 Balance hands-on production responsibilities with review, mentorship, troubleshooting, and team support.
 Adapt plans and priorities when creative direction, production scope, technical requirements, or client feedback changes.
 Technical and Pipeline Responsibilities
 Partner with Technical Art and Engineering to ensure lighting solutions are visually effective, technically stable, and appropriate for the target platform.
 Work within established budgets for frame rate, dynamic lights, shadows, volumetrics, reflections, global illumination, memory, and scalability.
 Diagnose and resolve issues involving exposure, shadow artifacts, light leaking, reflections, global illumination, volumetrics, bake quality, material response, and post-processing.
 Determine when to use dynamic, baked, stationary, or hybrid lighting approaches based on project requirements.
 Profile lighting work and make informed visual tradeoffs to meet performance requirements.
 Validate lighting across relevant gameplay cameras, display settings, hardware targets, times of day, weather states, and scalability levels.
 Help develop and maintain reusable lighting setups, templates, documentation, validation processes, and best practices.
 Identify workflow inefficiencies and recommend practical improvements to Art Direction, Technical Art, or Production.
 Follow project standards for scene organization, naming conventions, source control, documentation, and asset integration.
 Cross-Discipline Collaboration
 Collaborate with Environment Art to ensure geometry, materials, composition, and set dressing support the intended lighting.
 Partner with VFX to integrate fog, particles, weather, fire, emissive effects, and atmospheric elements.
 Work with Design to ensure lighting supports navigation, player guidance, combat readability, objectives, and interactive systems.
 Coordinate with Character Art and Animation to maintain readable and appealing character presentation in gameplay and cinematics.
 Partner with Cinematics teams on shot composition, continuity, exposure, character lighting, and narrative focus.
 Communicate artistic and technical tradeoffs clearly to both creative and non-creative stakeholders.
 Work effectively with distributed teams, partner studios, external vendors, and clients across different time zones.
 Requirements
 Professional experience creating lighting for games, real-time projects, or a closely related field.
 At least one shipped game or comparable professional real-time project.
 A portfolio or reel demonstrating high-quality real-time lighting.
 Strong understanding of lighting fundamentals, including value, color, contrast, composition, visual hierarchy, atmosphere, exposure, shadow, and material response.
 Experience lighting gameplay environments and interactive real-time scenes.
 Strong understanding of how lighting supports mood, gameplay readability, navigation, environmental storytelling, and player focus.
 Professional experience using Unreal Engine or another modern real-time engine.
 Experience with dynamic and baked lighting, global illumination, reflections, volumetrics, exposure, color grading, and post-processing.
 Working knowledge of physically based rendering, material response, tone mapping, and high-dynamic-range lighting.
 Understanding of real-time lighting optimization, including light cost, shadow complexity, volumetrics, reflections, memory, scalability, and platform constraints.
 Experience taking ownership of lighting for a level, scene, sequence, environment, or comparable area of production.
 Experience reviewing the work of other artists and providing clear, actionable feedback.
 Ability to identify when work does not meet the established quality bar and communicate what is required to improve it.
 Demonstrated ability to balance artistic quality, technical limitations, production scope, and schedule requirements.
 Ability to solve artistic and technical problems with limited supervision.
 Strong written, verbal, presentation, and interpersonal communication skills.
 Experience collaborating with Art Direction, Environment Art, Technical Art, VFX, Design, Engineering, Production, or Cinematics.
 Ability to organize priorities, communicate risks, and follow work through to completion.
 Ability to adapt to different projects, visual styles, engines, pipelines, platforms, and client expectations.
 Comfort participating in internal and client-facing art reviews.
 Tools and Technical Experience
 Candidates should have strong experience with a professional real-time lighting toolset. This may include:
 Unreal Engine 5 or another modern real-time engine
 Lumen or comparable real-time global-illumination systems
 GPU Lightmass, CPU Lightmass, or comparable baked-lighting systems
 Real-time profiling, visualization, and debugging tools
 Photoshop or comparable image-editing software
 DaVinci Resolve, Nuke, After Effects, or comparable color and compositing tools
 Maya, Blender, 3ds Max, or another 3D content-creation package
 Perforce or another production source-control system
 Jira, Confluence, Miro, or comparable planning and documentation tools
 Expertise with every listed application is not required. We are primarily interested in candidates who demonstrate strong lighting fundamentals, production judgment, technical adaptability, and the ability to learn project-specific tools.
 Preferred Qualifications
 Experience working in co-development, outsourcing, consulting, or work-for-hire game production.
 Experience contributing to AAA PC or console titles.
 Experience working across both realistic and stylized visual pipelines.
 Previous experience acting as a lighting point person, feature owner, task lead, or senior reviewer.
 Experience coordinating the work of other artists without formal management authority.
 Experience working with remote teams, partner studios, or external vendors.
 Experience owning the lighting for a level, biome, world region, cinematic sequence, or major gameplay feature.
 Advanced Unreal Engine knowledge, including Lumen, Nanite, Virtual Shadow Maps, volumetric fog, reflection systems, exposure controls, post-process volumes, lighting channels, and scalability settings.
 Experience with dynamic time-of-day systems, weather systems, destructible environments, or changing gameplay states.
 Experience lighting cinematics, characters, dialogue scenes, or scripted sequences in a real-time engine.
 Knowledge of cinematography, photography, film lighting, camera exposure, lens behavior, and color science.
 Experience with HDR displays, tone mapping, platform calibration, accessibility considerations, or multiple display formats.
 Familiarity with rendering pipelines, shader behavior, material development, and image-based lighting.
 Familiarity with Blueprints, Python, editor scripting, automation, or technical-art workflows.
 Experience creating lighting documentation, templates, validation tools, or review processes.
 Experience participating in estimates, staffing discussions, hiring reviews, portfolio evaluations, or art tests.
 Portfolio Requirements
 Your portfolio or reel should demonstrate:
 High-quality real-time lighting with strong composition, mood, color, contrast, readability, atmosphere, and scene cohesion.
 Work presented in a commercial, proprietary, or modern real-time engine.
 Clear explanations of your individual contribution, responsibilities, workflow, and production decisions.
 Gameplay lighting that guides attention, supports navigation, and reinforces the intended player experience.
 Effective integration between lighting, environments, materials, VFX, atmosphere, characters, and post-processing.
 An understanding of optimization, scalability, technical limitations, and production constraints.
 Examples showing ownership of lighting from initial direction or blockout through final delivery.
 The ability to work from concept art, reference, environment blockouts, narrative direction, gameplay requirements, or incomplete creative direction.
 Adaptability across different projects, genres, visual styles, or lighting conditions.
 We also encourage applicants to include:
 Day and night treatments of the same environment.
 Dynamic and baked lighting examples.
 Lighting created for different gameplay states, weather conditions, or times of day.
 Before-and-after comparisons showing how lighting improved readability, mood, composition, or performance.
 Examples of scenes that were reviewed or completed under your guidance, with your responsibilities clearly explained.
 Lighting guides, benchmark scenes, review notes, color scripts, documentation, or templates created for other artists.
 Please clearly identify your individual contribution to collaborative work.
 How to Apply
 A resume and portfolio or reel link are required.
 Please include shipped-game credits or comparable professional project experience where applicable. Candidates may be asked to participate in a portfolio review, technical discussion, leadership interview, or art assessment as part of the selection process.

 Avis d’offre d’emploi (vivier de talents)
Notez que cette offre d’emploi n’est pas associée à un poste actuellement vacant.  Nous cherchons un(e) artiste senior en éclairage pour créer des éclairages en temps réel d’excellente qualité et pour guider à la mise en œuvre de l’éclairage sur l’ensemble des projets GameSim.
 Il s’agit d’un rôle senior concret avec des responsabilités de leadership. En plus de produire du travail d’éclairage, vous réviserez le travail d’autres artistes, fournirez des directives claires et des commentaires, vous aiderez à l’organisation des tâches d’éclairage et vous vous assurerez que les scènes répondent aux exigences de qualité visuelles et techniques établies par la direction artistique et le client.
 Vous collaborerez étroitement avec les directeurs artistiques, les artistes en environnements, les artistes techniques, les artistes en effets visuels, les concepteurs, les ingénieurs, les producteurs, les clients et les studios partenaires. Vous aiderez à traduire la direction créative en solutions d’éclairage concrètes qui renforcent l’ambiance, la lisibilité du jeu, la narration environnementale, la narration et la performance.
 Ce poste peut impliquer la supervision du travail quotidien d’autres artistes en éclairage ou d’artistes pluridisciplinaires qui contribuent à la conception de l’éclairage. Il n’implique pas nécessairement de responsabilités officielles de gestion du personnel, mais exige de rendre compte des résultats de l’équipe, d’assurer un accompagnement efficace et de signaler tout problème lorsque le travail risque de ne pas répondre aux attentes en matière de qualité, d’échéances ou d’aspects techniques.
 Définition du succès
 Au cours de vos 90 premiers jours de travail…
 Vous développerez une bonne compréhension de la direction visuelle du projet, des exigences en matière de jouabilité, du pipeline de l’éclairage, des contraintes techniques et du calendrier de production.
 Vous établirez des relations de travail avec les équipes de la direction artistique, de la production, de l’art technique, de l’art environnemental, de la conception et de l’ingénierie, ainsi qu’avec des clients et d’autres équipes partenaires.
 Vous créerez un travail d’éclairage soigné qui démontre la qualité visuelle et technique attendue pour le projet.
 Vous prendrez en charge l’éclairage pour les niveaux, les environnements, les séquences ou les groupes de scènes qui vous sont attribués.
 Vous réviserez les travaux d’autres artistes et leur fournirez des commentaires opportuns et concrets qui améliorent la qualité et la cohérence.
 Vous identifierez les risques artistiques, techniques et de production aussi tôt que possible, travaillerez avec la direction du projet pour les résoudre.
 Vous aiderez l’équipe à réaliser des tâches d’éclairage qui répondent aux attentes fixées pour chaque étape en matière de qualité, de performance et d’exhaustivité.
 Responsabilités
 Création et mise en œuvre artistique de l’éclairage
 Créer des éclairages de grande qualité en temps réel pour les environnements, les niveaux, les cinématiques, les personnages et les séquences interactives du jeu.
 Traduire la direction artistique, l’art conceptuel, la documentation, les exigences en matière de jouabilité, les objectifs narratifs et les commentaires des clients en solutions d’éclairage efficaces.
 Utiliser l’éclairage pour établir l’ambiance, l’atmosphère, la hiérarchie visuelle et la narration environnementale, et pour guider la concentration du joueur.
 S’assurer que l’éclairage facilite la lisibilité du jeu, la navigation, la visibilité des combats, la présentation des personnages et les éléments interactifs importants.
 Développer et affiner l’exposition, les couleurs, les contrastes, le brouillard, l’atmosphère, les reflets, les ombres, la lumière émissive, la gradation de couleur et le post-traitement.
 Créer des éclairages pour une grande variété de styles visuels, y compris des projets réalistes, stylisés et cinématiques, et des projets avec une direction artistique poussée.
 Veiller à la cohérence entre les environnements, les espaces de jouabilité, les cinématiques, les moments de la journée, les conditions météorologiques et les scénarios d’éclairage interconnectés.
 Prendre en charge les scènes assignées pour les faire parvenir à la qualité finale, tout en respectant les exigences techniques et les échéances de la production.
 Supervision de la qualité et leadership
 Superviser les tâches d’éclairage pour la partie assignée du projet, comme un niveau, une région du monde, une séquence, une fonctionnalité ou une étape.
 Passez en revue le travail des artistes en éclairage et des autres intervenants dont le travail affecte le résultat final en matière d’éclairage.
 Fournir des commentaires clairs, constructifs et concrets par l’intermédiaire d’évaluations en direct, de remarques écrites, de repeintures, de tableaux de référence, de documentation ou d’exemples dans le moteur.
 S’assurer que le travail d’éclairage respecte la direction visuelle, les normes techniques et les attentes en matière de qualité établies par la direction artistique et le client.
 Aider les artistes à comprendre les priorités, les résultats attendus, les critères d’acceptation et le niveau de finition requis pour chaque jalon.
 Effectuer le suivi de la progression visuelle des tâches d’éclairage assignées et identifier des scènes qui nécessitent de l’assistance supplémentaire, une révision ou une priorité.
 Vérifier que les commentaires ont été pris en compte et que le travail réalisé répond aux critères de qualité établis avant de le soumettre.
 Accompagner les artistes juniors et intermédiaires dans les bases de l’éclairage, la mise en œuvre technique, l’organisation des scènes, l’optimisation et les pratiques de production.
 Montrer l’exemple avec une mise en œuvre artistique solide, une communication professionnelle, un suivi fiable et des résolutions de problèmes concrètes.
 Aider à résoudre les divergences d’opinions artistiques en référant les décisions aux cibles visuelles approuvées, aux besoins de la jouabilité, aux contraintes techniques et aux priorités du projet.
 Porter les problèmes non résolus liés à la qualité, au champ d’application, au personnel, aux échéances ou aux risques techniques à l’attention des gestionnaires de projets et d’équipes.
 Soutien à la planification et à la production
 Collaborer avec les équipes de direction artistique et de production afin de décomposer les objectifs d’éclairage en tâches claires, en priorités, en estimations et en jalons livrables.
 Aider à évaluer le champ d’application de l’éclairage, la complexité des scènes, les interdépendances et les risques de production.
 Assister à l’attribution des tâches en fonction des forces des artistes, des priorités du projet et des contraintes d’échéance.
 Fournir des mises à jour sur la progression et aviser lorsque des tâches risquent fort de ne pas respecter les attentes visuelles ou techniques, ou une échéance.
 Participer aux examens quotidiens, aux évaluations de jalon, aux révisions des clients et aux discussions pour la planification du projet.
 Aider à la préparation des tâches d’éclairage en vue des révisions internes, des présentations aux clients, des livraisons de jalons et de la livraison finale.
 Concilier les responsabilités concrètes de la production avec la révision, l’accompagnement, le dépannage et l’assistance à l’équipe.
 Adapter les plans et les priorités lorsque la direction créative, le champ d’application, les exigences techniques ou les commentaires des clients changent.
 Responsabilités techniques et liées au pipeline
 Collaborer avec les équipes de l’art technique et de l’ingénierie pour s’assurer que les solutions d’éclairage sont visuellement efficaces, techniquement stables et adaptées à la plateforme cible.
 Travailler en respectant les budgets fixés pour la fréquence d’image, les lumières dynamiques, les ombres, les effets volumétriques, les reflets, l’éclairage global, la mémoire et l’évolutivité.
 Diagnostiquer les problèmes liés à l’exposition, aux artefacts d’ombre, aux fuites de lumière, aux reflets, à l’éclairage global, à la volumétrie, à la qualité du précalcul, à la réponse des matériaux et au post-traitement, et résoudre ces problèmes.
 Déterminer quand utiliser des approches d’éclairage dynamiques, précalculés, fixes ou hybrides en fonction des exigences du projet.
 Profiler les tâches d’éclairages et effectuer des compromis visuels réfléchis afin de répondre aux exigences de performance.
 Vérifier l’éclairage pour l’ensemble des caméras de jeu concernées, des paramètres d’affichage, des cibles matérielles, des moments de la journée, des conditions météorologiques et des niveaux d’évolutivité.
 Aider à développer et maintenir des configurations d’éclairage réutilisables, des modèles, de la documentation, des processus de validation et de meilleures pratiques.
 Identifier les inefficacités dans les flux de travail et proposer des améliorations concrètes aux équipes de direction artistique, d’art technique ou de production.
 Respecter les normes du projet pour l’organisation des scènes, les conventions de nomenclature, le contrôle des versions, la documentation et l’intégration des actifs.
 Collaboration interdisciplinaire

 Infrastructure includes the foundational systems that shape our quality of life: water, transportation, transit, roads and highways, broadband, and power. It represents a multi-trillion-dollar market and a 20+ year megatrend in North America.

The platform integrates seamlessly with CRMs, ERPs, and data lakes, embedding actionable insights directly into sales workflows so teams can prioritize the right pursuits and build stronger pipelines.

 This role requires a strong command of data engineering best practices, a track record with orchestration and data warehouses, and hands-on experience shipping LLM and agentic workflows to production. You'll own the design, build, and operation of production data pipelines that use AI to power customer-facing solutions. You'll work with technologies we already use, including GCP services like Cloud Composer, Cloud SQL, BigQuery, and Vertex AI.

 Proficiency in Python and SQL.
 Proven experience (3+ years) working as a Data Engineer or Software Engineer in a cloud environment.

 Excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently on ambiguous problems.

 Job Description
 Location: Remote — United States, Canada, or United Kingdom only
 Compensation: $145,000–$180,000 OTE
 ABOUT TRIVIUM
 Trivium Group is an Inc. 5000-ranked, Clutch Award-winning Amazon growth agency. We manage millions in ad spend and help brands scale profitably on the world's most competitive marketplace. Our closers don't take orders — they own the number. This is a small, high-performing team.
 THE ROLE
 This is a full sales cycle seat, not a closer-only seat.
 Qualified leads come to you. Demand is inbound heavy, generated through our own paid marketing across Amazon, Meta and Google, so warm leads land on your calendar — you don't have to find it. But if your calendar is light, you do not sit and wait. You work the list, you set your own calls, and you get the deal on the books. We are hiring someone hungry: someone who sees a lead and lets nothing get in the way of closing it and collecting the cash.
 You own the deal end to end: outreach and call-setting when needed, discovery, audit review, proposal, objection handling, close, and cash collection. Deals are monthly retainers in the $3,000–$7,000/month range, sold to e-commerce owners and operators.
 Who you'll be selling to: e-commerce entrepreneurs whose businesses range from a couple million a year to a couple million a month. You need to be able to hold a sales conversation with them as a peer — without pedestalizing them.
 YOUR NUMBER
 Cash collected is the #1 KPI. Not calls booked, not proposals sent, not pipeline created — cash collected. Close rate, average deal size, speed to close, and pipeline hygiene all support that one number.
 WHAT YOU'LL DO
 • Run the full cycle on inbound and referred demand — first call to signature to payment.
 • Set your own calls when the calendar has room. Follow up relentlessly on no-shows, stalls, and old leads.
 • Diagnose a prospect's e-commerce business live on the call and connect it to what we do.
 • Build and present proposals for monthly retainers, handle objections, and get signatures.
 • Own collection — a signed deal that doesn't pay is not a closed deal.
 • Keep the CRM clean and current: every deal, every next step, every dollar.
 • Work with the delivery team so what you sell is what gets delivered.
 WHO THIS IS NOT FOR
 • You only work leads that are already on your calendar.
 • You need a manager to tell you what to do each morning.
 • You cut corners on admin — CRM notes, Slack updates, end-of-day reports.
 • Your experience is one-call, one-time-payment consumer sales with no retainer track record.
 • You avoid the money conversation.
 OUTCOMES & KPIS
 Steady state, after ramp:
 • $30,000+ in new MRR cash collected per month, minimum.
 • 6–8 closed retainers per month, at a $4,000–$5,000/month average deal size.
 • 100% of signed deals paid — a signed deal that doesn't pay is not a closed deal.
 • 25%+ live call close rate (calls held to signed).
 • Speed to close: first call to signature within 14 days on qualified deals.
 • Average deal size held at or above $4,000/month.
 • Supported by 4–5 qualified calls a day, 5 days a week (about 100 held calls a month), with enough open calendar space to absorb full inbound demand and self-set calls when the calendar is light.
 TIME & LOCATION
 • Full time, 30–40 hours a week, with freedom to build your own schedule — as long as there's enough open calendar space to hold 4–5 calls a day.
 • Available on Slack during core US business hours daily.
 WHAT YOU NEED
 This is a senior, high-trust seat, and we are being deliberately selective.
 • A track record closing recurring retainers in the $3,000–$7,000/month range (or higher), with numbers you can show: average deal size, close rate, cash collected.
 • Full sales cycle experience — you have set your own meetings, not just taken handed-off calls.
 • E-commerce experience is mandatory. You understand the numbers behind an e-commerce business, including CAC, LTV and funnel optimization.
 • Hands-on familiarity with at least one of: Amazon Ads, Facebook/Meta Ads, or Google Ads. You don't have to run campaigns, but you must hold a credible performance conversation.
 • B2B agency sales experience.
 • Based in the US, Canada, or UK, working US business hours.
 • A self-starter. That includes proactively studying — advertising, e-commerce, and B2B sales, daily.
 • Detailed and punctual. Our system is operations heavy: a clean and updated CRM, Slack, end-of-day reports, and the rest of the process are non-negotiable.
 • Comfortable being measured in public: cash collected, close rate, and pipeline hygiene are all visible.
 WHAT MAKES YOU STAND OUT
 • You've sold for an Amazon, Meta, Google, or TikTok performance agency.
 • You can read an ad account or P&L and speak to it live on a call.
 • You've carried a quota where the deal was a monthly commitment, not a one-time payment.
 • You've built pipelines from a cold list when inbound went quiet — and it worked.
 • You're coachable on our process and still bring your own frame to a call.
 COMPENSATION & BENEFITS
 • $145,000–$180,000 OTE.
 • 100% remote — work from anywhere in the US, Canada or UK.

Job Description 
 What is the opportunity? 
 The Senior Director, Data Architecture simplifies and unifies RBC's data architecture across the full lifecycle: manufacturing, distribution, discovery, consumption and governance. They own the target data architecture, the RBC Lumina reference architecture and the standards that make data machine-readable for people, applications and AI agents.
 Success means fewer data stores and point-to-point feeds, one trusted source for each critical data element, and data products agents can find and use within their entitlements.
 What will you do? 
 Manufacturing (data sources). Name the authoritative source for every critical data element. Own the canonical data model and business glossary alignment. Set the standard for producer data contracts covering schema, semantics, quality rules and SLAs, so quality is fixed at the source.
 Distribution (RBC Lumina). Own the Lumina reference architecture and the standard ingestion patterns: batch, streaming, CDC, events and APIs. Move data once, reliably and traceably. Run the roadmap to retire point-to-point interfaces.
 Discovery and machine readability. Define what counts as a data product and the minimum metadata each must carry: meaning, owner, lineage, quality and entitlements. Build the semantic layer and ontology that lets agents interpret data, not just locate it. Set the agent-access pattern for data products, such as MCP.
 Consumption. Define the consumption archetypes (BI, operational APIs, analytics and ML, RAG, agents) with one supported pattern for each. Feed curated, entitlement-aware data products into the common RAG substrate.
 Governance by design. Act as design authority through architecture review, decision records and exceptions. Partner with the CDO, who owns policy and accountability, while this role owns how standards are built in. Support BCBS 239 lineage and jurisdiction-aware data placement for sovereignty.
 Simplification and transformation. Inventory data platforms, stores and tools across RBC's stacks and give each a disposition: tolerate, invest, migrate or eliminate. Tie the roadmap to in-flight programs such as Finance Modernization and AML Transformation, and to third-party rationalization.
 What do you need to succeed? 
 15+ years in data architecture or data engineering, including 5+ years leading architects at enterprise scale.
 Depth across lakehouse and warehouse platforms, streaming and CDC, data products and mesh, catalogs and metadata, semantic layers and knowledge graphs.
 A track record of measurable simplification: platforms retired, feeds removed and costs taken out.
 Working knowledge of BCBS 239, privacy regulation and OSFI expectations for data risk.
 Clear view on making data AI-ready, including retrieval, entitlement propagation and agent access.
 Able to align the CDO, platform engineering and business data owners without direct authority over them.
